newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro zone may seek progress on tax -Trichet quoted.
newsitem.headline: Euro zone may seek progress on tax -Trichet quoted.

text.p: Countries inside European monetary union may show progress in harmonising taxes after the launch of the euro, though any decision will depend on all European Union members, Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet was quoted on Thursday as telling a parliamentary committee.
Trichet attended the hearing, of the parliament's finance committee, on Wednesday.

"He noted that tax harmonisation was a delicate problem, all the more so in that it required unanimity at the European Council (of all European Union members), but he said countries in the euro zone might perhaps show a political will to make progress in this area," the minutes quoted him as saying.
He had been asked by a member of parliament about the need for a discussion on the social and fiscal implications of the introduction of Europe's single currency in January, 1999.

The question of trying to bring taxation more into line among countries in the European Union has raised fears in some quarters, notably in Britain, of an extension of EU powers over national sovereignty.
European Union members have for years looked informally at ways of bringing taxation into line to avoid encouraging money to flow into one country and out of the other, so far without success.
